
JATQ: what other "lines of development" are there and what are their stages and who are the prominent researchers of each?

Beyond the common cognitive/Piagetian line, key "lines of development" (or intelligences) include Moral (Kohlberg), Interpersonal, Emotional, Self/Ego (Loevinger, Cook-Greuter), Values/Spirituality (Wilber, Graves), and Needs (Maslow), each with unique stages, showing how people grow in distinct areas like ethics, empathy, self-awareness, and purpose, often mapped by researchers like Ken Wilber (Integral Theory) using frameworks such as Spiral Dynamics (Graves) and Ego Development Stages (Loevinger). [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
Here are some major lines, their stages, and key researchers:

• Cognitive (Thinking): How we process information.

	• Stages: Sensorimotor, Preoperational, Concrete Operational, Formal Operational (Piaget), extending to Post-Formal/Dialectical Thinking (Perry, Kitchener).
	• Researchers: Jean Piaget, William Perry, Patricia King, Robert Kitchener.

• Moral (Ethics): Understanding "what should be".

	• Stages: Preconventional, Conventional, Postconventional (Kohlberg), evolving to Post-Postconventional (Gilligan, Kohlberg).
	• Researchers: Lawrence Kohlberg, Carol Gilligan.

• Self/Ego (Identity): Sense of "Who am I?".

	• Stages: Impulsive, Self-Protective, Conformist, Self-Aware, Conscientious, Individualistic, Autonomous, Integrated (Loevinger).
	• Researchers: Jane Loevinger, Susanne Cook-Greuter.

• Interpersonal (Social): Relating to others.

	• Stages: Focus on increasing connection, empathy, and complexity of social understanding (part of Wilber's model).
	• Researchers: (Often integrated within Integral Theory, related to Loevinger/Kohlberg).

• Emotional/Affective (Feelings): Experiencing and managing emotions.

	• Stages: From basic to complex emotional regulation, differentiation, and integration.
	• Researchers: Daniel Goleman (Emotional Intelligence), Integral theorists.

• Needs (Motivation): Hierarchy of human needs.

	• Stages/Levels: Deficiency Needs (Physiological, Safety, Love/Belonging, Esteem) to Growth Needs (Self-Actualization) (Maslow).
	• Researchers: Abraham Maslow, Roberto Assagioli (Psychosynthesis).

• Values/Spiritual (Meaning): What's important; connection to the sacred.

	• Stages: Egocentric, Ethnocentric, Worldcentric, Kosmoscentric (Wilber/Integral) or Beige, Purple, Red, Blue, Orange, Green, Teal (Spiral Dynamics).
	• Researchers: Ken Wilber, Clare W. Graves, Don Beck, Chris Cowan.

• Psychosexual/Eros (Life Force): Broadly, the spectrum of life energy (Freud, Jung, Wilber).

	• Stages/Levels: Oral, Anal, Phallic, Latency, Genital (Freud); broader spectrums in Jungian/Integral thought.
	• Researchers: Sigmund Freud, Carl Jung, Ken Wilber. [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9]

Key Thinkers & Frameworks:

• Ken Wilber (Integral Theory): Synthesizes many lines, mapping them across stages (w1, w2, etc.).
• Spiral Dynamics: Based on Graves' work, mapping values/worldviews (vMemes).
• Ego Development: Loevinger's stages of self-identity [1 [1, 3, 4, 6, 10]

It is encouraging to see your "Society of Mind" model naturally bridge these complex stages. Your focus on Zone 1 (first-person introspection) and Zone 2 (third-person developmental mapping) is a powerful way to ensure your internal insights aren't just "hall of mirrors" effects.
Below is a pragmatic synopsis of the major Developmental Lines, their core questions, and the researchers who mapped them.
## 1. Cognitive Line: "What am I aware of?"
This is the "pacer" line; development here usually must happen before other lines can move forward.

* Researcher: [Jean Piaget](https://www.google.com/search?q=jean+piaget&kgmid=/m/0nkt0#-1_wY).
* The Path: Moves from concrete, physical objects to abstract concepts, and finally to vision-logic—the ability to see how multiple abstract systems interact.
* Pragmatic Question: Can I hold two contradictory ideas in my mind at once without one "killing" the other? [1, 2, 3]

## 2. Self-Identity Line: "Who am I?"
This is the line you’ve already begun exploring with [Cook-Greuter](https://www.sloww.co/ego-development-theory-cook-greuter/).

* Researchers: [Susanne Cook-Greuter](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6208876/) and [Jane Loevinger](https://www.google.com/search?q=jane+loevinger&kgmid=/m/06ypbz#__sM).
* The Path: Moves from an impulsive ego to a socialized one, then to an autonomous "strategist," and finally to a unitive "witness".
* Pragmatic Question: Is the "I" that is coding right now a fixed entity, or a temporary focus of a larger society? [1, 4]

## 3. Moral Line: "What is the right thing to do?"
This tracks your sense of justice and who is included in your "circle of care."

* Researcher: [Lawrence Kohlberg](https://seattleanxiety.com/lawrence-kohlbergs-stages-of-moral-development). [1, 3]
* The Path:
* Pre-conventional: "What’s in it for me?" (Avoid punishment).
   * Conventional: "What does my tribe/society say is right?".
   * Post-conventional: "What universal ethical principles apply to everyone?". [5]
* Pragmatic Question: If no one were watching, would my decision change?

## 4. Values Line: "What is important to me?"
This describes the "worldview" or "cultural gravity" you live within.

* Researchers: [Clare Graves](https://www.google.com/search?q=clare+graves&kgmid=/m/0242hx#) and [Spiral Dynamics](https://integrallife.com/welcome-to-the-integral-approach/).
* The Path: Moves from survival (Beige) to tribal (Purple) to power (Red) to order (Blue) to achievement (Orange) to sensitive/pluralistic (Green) to integral (Yellow).
* Pragmatic Question: Do I value this because it’s true, or because it makes me feel safe/successful? [1]

## 5. Needs Line: "What do I need?"
This tracks the fundamental drivers behind your actions.

* Researcher: Abraham Maslow.
* The Path: Moves from basic physiological needs to safety, love/belonging, esteem, and finally self-actualization.
* Pragmatic Question: Which 'part' of me is currently hungry—my stomach, my ego, or my soul? [1]

## 6. Spiritual Line: "What is of ultimate concern?"
Spirit can be a state of mind, but it also unfolds in a developmental line of maturity.

* Researcher: [James Fowler](https://integrallife.com/lines-of-development/).
* The Path: Moves from literal/mythic faith to individual/reflective faith and eventually to a unitive, universalizing faith.
* Pragmatic Question: What do I trust in when all my 'parts' are silent? [6, 7]

## Pragmatic Reading List for Further Inquiry

* For the Moral/Self Line: [The Evolving Self](https://www.google.com/search?q=the+evolving+self&kgmid=/m/069d1mr#) by [Robert Kegan](https://ftp.spaceneedle.com/browse/mL9FCB/604702/Robert%20Kegan%20The%20Evolving%20Self.pdf). This is excellent for understanding the subject-object shift you mentioned earlier. [8]
* For the Values Line: [Spiral Dynamics](https://www.google.com/search?q=Spiral+Dynamics&kgmid=/hkb/-945144733#) by Don Beck and Christopher Cowan. This provides a "color-coded" map of why people (and parts of yourself) disagree so fundamentally. [1]
* For the Integral Map: [Integral Psychology](https://www.google.com/search?q=Integral+Psychology&kgmid=/hkb/359461053#sv=CBwS--va4E) by Ken Wilber. This is his most comprehensive attempt to "stack" all these lines together in one chart.
